product: Solid-oxide fuel cell Energy Servers for on-site data center power. Oracles Project Jupiter will use Bloom fuel cells for up to 2.45 GW, replacing planned gas turbines and diesel generators (Oracle newsroom and PR Newswire, 2026-04-27). CEO calls Bloom a standard for AI onsite power (SEC 8-K, 2026-07-28).
demand: Volume-led. Q2 2026 product revenue rose 215.4 percent YoY to $935.4M versus total revenue up 165.5 percent to $1.065B (SEC 8-K, 2026-07-28); installation grew 36 percent and service 27 percent, so system volume drives growth, not price, with mix tilting to data-center products.
pricing_power: Scandium-oxide cost spikes, natural-gas and tariff costs, loss or reduction of IRA and OBBBA tax credits, and turbine or genset price competition. Also customer concentration (2.4 GW Oracle) and the shift to a consult-only installation model (risk factors, SEC 8-K, 2026-07-28). FY26 guidance assumes about 34 percent non-GAAP gross margin.
competition: No Chinese low-cost fuel-cell substitute was evidenced. The China exposure is upstream, in the scandium-oxide dopant: Bloom says it recovers scandium from titanium, nickel, cobalt and uranium byproducts, is not China-dependent, and has other materials that can perform a similar role (company blog and SEC 8-K, 2026-07-09). The class action alleges the opposite.

web_who_loses: Combustion and grid incumbents: gas-turbine and diesel-genset makers such as GE Vernova, Siemens Energy and Cummins. Bloom states customers who traditionally defaulted to combustion technologies now proactively choose Bloom (CEO, SEC 8-K, 2026-07-28); Oracle replaced planned turbines and diesel at Project Jupiter (PR Newswire, 2026-04-27).
